newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Krupp says EMU delay makes no sense.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Krupp says EMU delay makes no sense.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Tuesday that it made no sense to delay the start date for Europe's economic and monetary union.

"A delay would be a particularly senseless measure. It has no economic advantages but only disadvantages. If we wait until fiscal criteria can be fulfilled because of an improved economic situation, we will win nothing, since the risks to stability are obviously larger in a boom," said Krupp.
Krupp was addressing a conference organised by the OeTV public sector and transport union.
"(In this decision) the sustainability of the situation achieved will play a larger role than any numbers after the comma," Krupp said in the text of a speech to be delivered at the conference.

Krupp was referring to the debate about whether the Maastricht treaty target for the ratio between a government's budget deficit and gross domestic product should be interpreted as precisely 3.0 percent or roughly three percent.

"It is...not right to use the Maastricht treaty and currency union to explain the current savings policy which we are experiencing in Germany at the moment which damages employment, as the German Finance Minister is doing," said Krupp.
"And the recent, failed, gold operation made clear once again the finance minister's improper approach to the fiscal criteria," Krupp said.
The Bundesbank and the German finance ministry were recently at loggerheads after the central bank signalled its opposition to government plans to revalue central bank assets.
Krupp said it was sensible to start EMU with a limited group of participants. Some pundits have called for a weakening of the Maastricht entry criteria and a wider initial membership.
